name: Alula Borealis
description: A star 122 parsecs away, 62 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 55219: radius 61.994 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1057.16 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.063) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 55219: effective temperature 4183 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.13)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 55219: distance 122.399 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.021), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 122 parsecs away, 62 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,057 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,183 K, so 61.994 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 55219: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Nu Ursae Majoris
quotes.card: Nu Ursae Majoris, formally named Alula Borealis, is a double star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Major.
quotes.introduction: At an apparent visual magnitude of +3.490, it is bright enough to be seen with the naked eye.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 757565233820538752 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
